entry_points.text: Trap/NMI zero fresh state, record CPU, vector, signal, error and registers, check reentry/readiness with auto-reboot bypass for non-trap faults, and request master. SysRq reports missing I/O, announces pending connection, then breaks, with help/action labels. Late init clears early mode, runs arch hook when ready, completes KDB init, and waits for a peer on early break.

exports.text: Address parser takes symbol/numeric with offset and env/register forms under a gate, returning address and offset. Helpers do text-to-unsigned, register check, string dup and gated print. Core lookup maps name to address and reverse to nearest symbol, searching names before modules and reverse core-first then module/BPF/ftrace by binary search, size from next address, and low/far cutoffs.

Registry rejects duplicate commands, appends otherwise; macro mode appends or registers on terminator, else unimplemented. Grep takes a pipe segment with quoted patterns and anchors into global filter state. Remote handlers select threads from hex ids, install/remove software/hardware breakpoints after validation, and pass or detach exceptions with error packets on failure.

Trap classifies fault, switch, keyboard, NMI, breakpoint and step, prepares bp/pager state, skips interaction on deferred-step resume, then reinstalls and selects resume, flagging missing peers. Main loop holds secondaries, maps outcomes to switch/step/remote/depart and drains keyboard. Cross-CPU stack is local-direct or via handshake. KDB init runs once level gated, clearing breakpoints and registering commands plus hardware support if present.

Registration validates, refuses duplicates and late boot consoles, prepares resources, resolves enablement, assigns sequence, inserts preferred-head, announces, retires boot consoles unless retained, and reconciles workers. Alloc checks callbacks, inits wait/deferred state, presets sequence, and gives shared boot or private buffers with threads; release syncs, stops and frees; stop is idempotent; fallback is no-op.

hazards.text: Folded string/list/memory helpers, no dossier. Argument buffers must be mutable for in-place splitting. Nearest-symbol uses a shared static buffer, nonreentrant. Low addresses bypass lookup; matches past eight mebibytes report none; reverse still yields empty output if ignored. Markers are dollar, percent, plus, minus, colon, pipe, quotes and anchors, with capped lengths.

Folded alloc, config, CPU, recovery and lockdown helpers, no dossier. Register form is unimplemented; missing context diagnoses; allocation can fail. Module-find is list-scan or latch-tree by config; BPF, build-id and section ends are opaque. Deep nesting panics after dropping breakpoints; faults or missing peers flag catastrophe. Keyboard drain may block; blanket enable must expand first; worker/enablement failures remove consoles; duplicates warn, late boot refused.

invariants.text: Lookup is colon-qualified single-module or unqualified scan over formed modules. Owner is null outside cached ranges or when unformed, with containment check. Reverse uses containing regions only, skips undefined/unnamed/mapping symbols, picks greatest at/below target and smallest above, deriving size/offset by difference under RCU without mutex.

Install is idempotent, clears delay unless deferred, defers with single-step when marked, else software for zero type or hardware with length/type; removal needs installed state. Reuse prefers removed slot at same address; full fails. Queries detect removed/active hits; init release clears init entries. Debug checks category bits; lockdown expands blanket enable then clears disallowed bits.

Enablement tries user, platform, then enabled, matching by driver else name/index under boot sync; Braille diverts. List keeps preferred head; removal unlinks deferred, transfers marking, recomputes flags, notifies and reconciles. Start uses syslog copy for replay/boot else next sequence with handover flush or lowest fallback, suppressing duplicates; status prefixes blocking and boot identity.

locks.text: List mutation needs the mutex, warning inside SRCU read; alloc, release, threads and reconcile assert ownership. Transitions use device guards; setup/handover use printing guard, syslog copy its guard, plus SRCU wait after unlink. Console writes mask interrupts; secondary/keyboard coordination spins relaxed. Module notifier succeeds; boot option registers once when ready.

External RCU, list, lockdep, interrupt-save/restore and atomic helpers underpin traversals, console output and CPU checks. Pass 1 names no dossier, so these sids fold as opaque dependencies; shown paths use read-side protection, held annotations and masked writes only.

state_machines.text: Legacy worker runs when legacy/boot consoles remain and forcing asks, else stops; failure removes blocking consoles. Nonblocking workers start when ready with no boot console and one such console each; failure removes it; running flag clears when boot returns or the last leaves. Reboot enters, detaches or ignores by mode; stub exit reports when connected outside KDB then disconnects.

structs.text: Console record has name, write routine, flags and index -1 with print-buffer plus enabled flags. Per-CPU info has entry, resume and exception bits with nesting tracked on active CPU. Keyboard drain waits for 9C skipping extended/repeat/mouse bytes, with a no-op build. History is a head/tail/nav ring; diagnostics map negatives via table; newline strips one LF; nav codes 16/14; register dump raises verbosity.
